lines: {target}? Sound travels farther than sense.
Before crossing sculk-covered stone where every step can carry, I would check every strap and loose tool.
Show me the cut you keep pretending not to notice.
An alert companion helps everyone by pointing out sculk clicking after a careless sound.
When the others are ready, I will listen to them too.
When you noticed sculk clicking after a careless sound, did everyone understand the warning?
The one who stayed calm may need comfort too.
Did someone keep watch while the others rested?
No one will laugh if you keep a lamp burning.
I will ask someone you trust to stay nearby.
Once you found a dry chamber with one guarded entrance, did anyone finally relax?
Careful plans need room for a shrieker calling something from the darkness, especially far from home.
Whatever sculk and ancient stone may be worth, it is less valuable than the person carrying it.
Your story gave Deep Dark a shape in my mind. I can almost see sculk spreading through deep stone.
The strongest traveler in the group still needs relief from cool damp underground air.
Give yourself a day before deciding what the journey meant.
I can replace supplies. I cannot replace a neighbor.
Your group survived whatever the sculk wakes by paying attention, not by boasting.
Take the bed nearest the door if that helps.
Good friends know when to stop pushing.
{target}? Pointed dripstone waits above and below every step.
Knowing cave mobs between sharp stone remained nearby must have made every sound harder to judge.
The world is strange enough without adding fear to every shadow.
Near Dripstone Caves, I would trust a dry chamber clear of falling dripstone only after checking every way in.
Show me the cut you keep pretending not to notice.
We are not sending anyone back tomorrow.
Smoke in the lungs can linger after courage returns.
I can replace supplies. I cannot replace a neighbor.
The door is shut. You can stop listening for footsteps.
Copper and dripstone gathered near marked paths can be found another day. A lost traveler cannot.
A warning carried home is worth more than a trophy.
Anyone bound for Dripstone Caves should hear about falling onto sharp dripstone before leaving.
The road can wait until your breathing settles.
Bad footing turns small injuries into serious trouble. I would treat Dark uneven cave floors with respect.
I would plan more rest than usual when facing damp cave air and constant dripping.
{target} sounds real to me now, especially the part about pointed stone hanging above dark pools.
Did anyone lose medicine along the road?
Did noticing water and echoes carrying through stone send you forward or turn you back?
It takes trust to pause and discuss water and echoes carrying through stone.
I can ask the baker to leave food by the meeting hall.
{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops.
How did you keep your footing across dark uneven cave floors?
The road can wait until your breathing settles.
Now when someone mentions Lush Caves, I will think first of dark stone opening into hidden chambers.
Good friends know when to stop pushing.
Even the quietest person may be the first to notice water and echoes carrying through stone.
Survival does not always feel like victory.
If part of the story is too much for tonight, leave it for morning.
The meeting place matters more than the prize.
There may be good uses for Moss, clay, and glow berries, though none justify ignoring a warning.
Let the fire burn a little brighter tonight.
A dry chamber with one guarded entrance would give an injured traveler a fair chance to recover.
Cool damp underground air can dull judgment before a traveler notices.
We are not sending anyone back tomorrow.
Which choice brought everyone home?
You were right to turn back when you did.
No treasure would make me dismiss a fall where the torchlight ends.
Did anyone speak after noticing water and echoes carrying through stone, or did you all simply listen?
It was wise to leave space between your party and cave mobs beyond the glow berries.
No one here needs you to pretend it was easy.
